news.headline: India bonds inch higher as oil steadies ahead of RBI verdict
news.summary: Indian government bonds have experienced a modest rise, driven by declining oil prices and consistent US Treasury yields. With the Reserve Bank of India's policy decision approaching, traders are treading carefully and shying away from large investments. The yield for the benchmark 2036 bond has dropped, suggesting a cautious market outlook.

news.headline: Axis Bank Share Price Live Updates: Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Allotment of ESOP / ESPS
US Treasury gains lift India bonds ahead of RBI meet
news.summary: On Wednesday, Indian government bonds rallied, influenced by a decrease in US Treasury yields. The benchmark 10-year bond yield fell to 7.1641%, marking a two-week low. The Indian rupee strengthened to its highest level for the fiscal year against the dollar. Overseas investors returned as net buyers of Indian debt, purchasing over 93 billion rupees. The Reserve Bank of India's upcoming decision will significantly affect market movements and trends.

news.headline: Shapoor Mistry lobbied Modi twice for Tata Sons IPO as battle over listing intensifies
news.summary: Shapoor Mistry, the head of the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, has reached out to Prime Minister Modi regarding the listing troubles faced by Tata Sons. He claims that Tata Trusts are obstructing the public offering for their own benefit and breaching regulations. Meanwhile, the Reserve Bank of India has pressured Tata Sons to meet listing necessities.

news.headline: Shift in pension and insurance money to equities dampens long-term G-sec demand: RBI DG
news.summary: The demand for long-term government securities has seen a marginal decline recently. Insurance companies and pension funds are increasingly focusing on equities instead of sovereign debt. This change has impacted the stability of the government securities market and highlighted challenges in liquidity distribution. The Reserve Bank of India emphasizes the need for a coordinated approach and broader participation from institutional investors.

news.headline: HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries among 10 stocks with highest DII holding in Q2. See full list
news.summary: With the rise in the share of MFs and also an overall net investment of Rs 1.69 lakh crore during the quarter, the share of Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) as a whole increased to an all-time high of 19.31% as on September 30, 2026, up from 19.16% as on June 30, 2026. Here are 10 stocks with the highest DII holding in the September quarter.

news.headline: India’s rupee has become an accidental carry star
news.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has made moves that temporarily attract carry traders to the rupee. Recent factors include decreasing oil prices and a shift in foreign investment from artificial intelligence stocks to Indian markets. However, these RBI incentives may not last, leaving uncertainty for traders. India's interest rate advantage has significantly diminished since 2011, raising concerns. Policymakers face challenges in ensuring sustained interest in the rupee amid historical depreciation.

news.headline: Fed policymakers at odds over causes of high inflation
news.summary: US inflation is expected to increase again in October, with potential implications for Federal Reserve interest rate decisions. Economists predict the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index to reach 3.8% this month. Analysts are divided regarding whether inflation is caused by demand or supply shocks stemming from recent policies. Market forecasts suggest three more rate hikes, signaling ongoing concerns about rising prices.

news.headline: Rupee pares FY27 losses, climbs 56 paise to 92.29/USD
news.summary: On Wednesday, the rupee reached an eight-month high against the US dollar amid foreign investments. This rise in value was supported by decreasing crude oil prices below USD 90 per barrel. The local currency opened at 92.65 but climbed to 92.29 during intraday trading. Foreign investors displayed confidence in Indian equities as indicated by significant net purchases on Monday.

news.headline: India pension funds pivot to bonds as equity exposure nears cap
news.summary: As India’s largest pension funds edge closer to the equity caps, a strategic pivot towards government bonds has been observed. UTI Pension Fund is channeling 50% of its new investments into government bonds, a marked increase from last year, while SBI Pension Funds aims to cut stock allocations to just 25%. This shift comes as markets rally, and a heightened bond focus could bolster India's debt market significantly.

news.headline: A 50 bps jumbo rate hike can lead to financial stability concerns, hurt growth: Report
news.summary: SBI economists have lowered their rate hike expectations for the upcoming RBI policy review. They now anticipate a 0.25 per cent increase rather than the previously expected 0.50 per cent. This adjustment stems from concerns regarding financial stability and potential impacts on economic growth. The RBI's monetary policy committee is scheduled to meet from December 2 to December 4.

news.headline: RBI DG asks primary dealers to bid responsibly in G-Sec underwriting auctions
news.summary: RBI Deputy Governor Rohit Jain has urged primary dealers to bid responsibly in government securities auctions. Jain noted instances of volatile pricing that misalign with orderly market conditions, impacting government borrowing costs. He highlighted the challenge of liquidity concentration in a few securities and called for improved market-making activities. Jain also pointed out declining demand from institutional investors for long-term sovereign debt amid uncertain interest rates.

news.headline: IIFCL IPO: Govt plans to sell part of its stake, company to issue fresh shares
news.summary: The government aims to partially divest its shareholding in India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd through an initial public offering. The IPO is expected to occur by the end of the current fiscal year, according to an official statement. IIFCL will issue fresh shares to raise capital alongside the government stake sale. The proceeds from the stake sale will contribute to the government's disinvestment revenue.

news.headline: Investors mint Rs 34.61 lakh cr in November as markets rally nearly 11%
news.summary: In a remarkable surge this month, Indian equity markets have observed a substantial upswing, with the BSE Sensex climbing nearly 11 percent. This rally was largely propelled by foreign institutional investors, who contributed record-setting inflows exceeding Rs 1 lakh crore. Motivated by lower crude oil prices and impressive Q2 earnings, investor optimism soared, although a recent profit booking saw a minor dip of nearly 2 percent.

news.headline: Dollar climbs as renewed AI euphoria fuels Fed hike bets
news.summary: The dollar is approaching a 20-month peak, thanks to the reinstatement of Nvidia's CEO, which has instilled confidence in the markets. Meanwhile, the euro and sterling struggle against the strong dollar, with the euro hovering near an 18-month low. The market forecasts a Fed rate hike, adjusting to anticipated shifts in monetary policy.
